# Feature: Auto-Generated Advance Sheet

> **Number**: 18.03.04
> **Parent**: [Show Advancing](./18.03-show-advancing-index.md)
> **Status**: [SURFACE]
> **Last updated**: 2026-07-16

## Overview

The one-page artifact that projects the settled advance for a date — schedule, contacts, tech
summary, accepted exceptions, backline, crew — generated from the advance rather than typed. Its
second job is strategic: it is the **escape hatch for venues that will never log in**, because a
PDF in an inbox still carries most of the value and requires zero adoption.

## Role Lens

| Role | Access | What They See/Do |
|------|--------|-------------------|
| Musician | Read-only | Rarely opens it — the day sheet (18.10) is their artifact. Sees it when they're the DIY act sending it themselves. |
| Producer | Full | Generates, previews, and sends. Chooses the recipient scope, exports PDF for the venue that won't sign up, and re-sends when the advance changes. |
| Operator | Read-only | The main recipient. Reads the sheet in an email, or in-app if they've adopted. Everything they need for the date on one page, with a link back to answer items. |
| Fan | None | Internal artifact. |

## Behavior

Generated from the settled (or in-progress) advance for one date, scoped by recipient — venue
production, local crew, the artist's team. Every version is stamped; a superseded sheet in an inbox
is the failure mode, so the sheet carries a version and a live link. The emailable path is
deliberately first-class, not a degraded fallback.

### Happy Path

1. Advance reaches settled; Producer opens the sheet — already assembled.
2. Producer previews the venue-scoped version and adds a note.
3. Producer sends: in-app to adopted venues, email + PDF to everyone else.
4. Operator reads it; the QR/short link lets them answer any remaining item without an account.
5. An advance change re-generates it and re-sends with a changed-lines summary.

### Edge Cases / Failure Modes

| Scenario | What Happens | User Sees |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Advance changes after the sheet was emailed | New version generated; old version marked superseded at the live link | Recipient at the old link: "Superseded — v4 is current" |
| Venue works from a printed copy | Version stamp + short link in the footer; nothing else can be done about paper | "v2 · wejamm.in/a/k3p9" |
| Sheet generated before the advance settles | Allowed but stamped as provisional, with open-item count | "PROVISIONAL — 7 items still open" |
| Venue replies to the email instead of using the link | Reply lands as an advance item thread if inbound mail is wired; otherwise lost | Producer: "Venue replied by email — 1 item to reconcile" |
| Recipient scope leaks (venue sheet includes crew pay) | Scoping is enforced at generation; a wrong-scope send is a confidentiality incident | Preview always shows "sending as: Venue view" |

### States

| State | Trigger | What User Sees |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| Loading | Sheet opened | Page skeleton |
| Empty | Advance not started | "Nothing to render — start the advance" |
| Populated | Advance has content | Scoped preview + send options |
| Error | Generation or send failed | "Couldn't send to [venue] — retry / download PDF" |
| Partial | Advance in progress | Provisional sheet with an open-item banner |

## Deep Think Annotations

| # | Hypothesis | Source | Outcome |
|---|-----------|--------|---------|
| DT-01 | This is a nice-to-have export | First-pass instinct | ❌ REJECTED — it is the **cold-start strategy for the whole domain**. The diff (18.03.02) needs venue data, and venue data needs Operator adoption, which cannot be assumed (18.03.01 DT-03). A sheet that lands in an inbox and lets a venue answer one item without an account is the lowest-friction on-ramp the domain has. It is a growth mechanism disguised as an export. |
| DT-02 | The advance sheet and the day sheet (18.10) are the same artifact | Near-duplicate check on the candidate list | ❌ REJECTED — different audience, timing and content. The advance sheet is venue-facing, weeks out, and *negotiates*; the day sheet is crew/band-facing, that morning, and *informs*. They share a render mechanism (recorded as a cross-cut), not an identity. Merging them would put per diems in a venue's inbox. |
| DT-03 | A sent PDF is a snapshot and that's acceptable | Naive modelling | ❌ REJECTED — a superseded sheet in an inbox is exactly how a venue ends up working to last week's schedule. Version stamp + live link + supersede notice at the old link is the minimum. Paper remains unsolvable; the version stamp is the only mitigation. |
| DT-04 | Inbound email replies should be parsed into items | Automation instinct | ⏳ DEFERRED — high value (venues *will* reply to the email) but real complexity and a spoofing surface. Flagged as Q-02 rather than assumed. |

## Decisions

| # | Decision | Context |
|---|----------|---------|
| D-01 | The emailable, no-account path is first-class, not a degraded fallback | It is the domain's cold-start on-ramp for Operator adoption |
| D-02 | Advance sheet and day sheet stay distinct artifacts sharing one render mechanism | Different audience, timing, and confidentiality scope |
| D-03 | Every sheet is versioned with a live link; the old link announces supersession | A snapshot in an inbox is how a venue works to last week's schedule |

## Open Questions

| # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
|---|----------|-------|-------------|
| Q-01 | How much can an account-less venue do via the link — read only, or answer items? The more they can do, the better the on-ramp and the larger the auth/spoofing surface. | User | `/create-prd-security` |
| Q-02 | Do we parse inbound email replies into advance items? High value, real spoofing risk. | User | `/create-prd` |
